title: Universality in the target arrival statistics of non-conservative search processes
summary: Stochastic search processes in which agents are continuously inserted into and removed from a target search domain are fundamental to a wide class of physical and artificial systems. The theory of such non-conservative search processes is, however, much less developed than for search processes with a fixed number of agents. Recent work on the non-conservative case has characterized the fastest first-passage time (FPT) to a target, after which the search process is terminated.
